text: Separating, and working out arrangements for your children? Here's a quick guide from Saltbush and Reed Family Law. Courts decide based on the child's best interests, including the safety of the child and the people who care for them. Since May 2024, the law no longer uses the term equal shared parental responsibility, often misread as equal time. Before applying to court, you usually need to try family dispute resolution, unless it isn't suitable, for example because of family violence. You can develop a parenting plan, and agreements can be formalised as consent orders. If you're separating, our team can help. Speak with Saltbush and Reed.
